original_question: Let (W1,S1) and (W2,S2) be Coxeter systems, and let u,v in W1 and w,z in W2 be such that the Bruhat intervals [u,v] and [w,z] are isomorphic as posets. Must the corresponding Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials agree, i.e. must P_{u,v}(q) = P_{w,z}(q)?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target almost exactly: it uses two Coxeter systems, assumes the two Bruhat intervals are isomorphic as posets, and asks whether the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials are equal. This is precisely the scope of Conjecture 1.4, not a broader neighboring problem.
missing_details: State explicitly that [u,v] and [w,z] are intervals in the Bruhat orders of W1 and W2.
Make explicit the comparability assumptions u ≤ v and w ≤ z, which are implicit in the interval notation.
Specify that P_{u,v}(q) and P_{w,z}(q) are the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of W1 and W2, namely the specialization P_{u,v} := P^{∅,-1}_{u,v} (= P^{∅,q}_{u,v}) in Z[q] from Theorem 1.3.
State the universal quantifier clearly: the question asks whether this equality holds for every pair of Coxeter systems and every pair of isomorphic Bruhat intervals.
For complete paper-faithfulness, identify the problem by name as the Combinatorial Invariance Conjecture.
refined_question: Combinatorial Invariance Conjecture: Let (W1,S1) and (W2,S2) be Coxeter systems, and let u ≤ v in W1 and w ≤ z in W2, where the intervals [u,v] := {x ∈ W1 : u ≤ x ≤ v} and [w,z] := {y ∈ W2 : w ≤ y ≤ z} are taken in Bruhat order. If [u,v] and [w,z] are isomorphic as posets, must the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of the two intervals coincide, i.e. must P_{u,v}(q) = P_{w,z}(q) in Z[q]?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, under the same hypotheses, must the ordinary R-polynomials agree: R_{u,v}(q) = R_{w,z}(q)?
justification: The draft is essentially Conjecture 1.4 verbatim. In Section 1 the paper first defines the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials by specializing the parabolic family in Theorem 1.3, with P_{u,v} = P^{∅,-1}_{u,v} (= P^{∅,q}_{u,v}), and similarly defines the ordinary R-polynomials from Theorem 1.2. It then states Conjecture 1.4 exactly for isomorphic Bruhat intervals as posets. The paragraph immediately following Conjecture 1.4 says that replacing the equality of Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials by the equality of R-polynomials gives an equivalent conjecture. So the only real improvements needed are to spell out Bruhat order, the meaning of interval notation, the ordinary/non-parabolic meaning of P_{u,v}, and the universal quantifiers. No extra hypotheses about type, field, characteristic, homogeneity, or degree restrictions belong to the conjecture itself.
